charges.name: Criminal Trespass
charges.maxPenalty: Class B misdemeanor: up to 180 days jail and/or $2,000 fine; Class A if on critical infrastructure

charges.name: Evading Arrest or Detention
charges.maxPenalty: Class A misdemeanor (on foot): up to 1 year jail and $4,000 fine; felony if in a vehicle

charges.name: Failure to Identify
charges.maxPenalty: Class C misdemeanor (refusal): up to $500 fine; Class B (false info): up to 180 days jail

charges.name: Criminal Mischief
charges.maxPenalty: Class C ($100 or less) to Class A ($2,500 or less): fines up to $4,000 and/or up to 1 year jail

charges.name: Terroristic Threat
charges.maxPenalty: Class B misdemeanor: up to 180 days jail and/or $2,000 fine; can be enhanced to felony

charges.name: Criminal Trespass
charges.maxPenalty: Up to 1 year jail and/or $1,000 fine

charges.name: Criminal Attempt
charges.maxPenalty: Varies — typically one class below the completed offense; up to life imprisonment for attempted first-degree felonies

charges.name: Criminal Conspiracy
charges.maxPenalty: Varies — typically same as or one class below the target offense; can be substantial even if the target crime was never completed

charges.name: Criminal Responsibility for Conduct of Another
charges.maxPenalty: Same as the principal offense — you face identical penalties to the person who directly committed the crime

charges.name: Hindering Apprehension or Prosecution
charges.maxPenalty: Typically a lower class felony than the underlying offense; federal carries up to half the sentence of the principal (18 U.S.C. § 3)

charges.name: Criminal Solicitation
charges.maxPenalty: Typically one class below the target offense; a felony solicitation can result in 1 to 10+ years imprisonment depending on the target crime

charges.name: Engaging in Organized Criminal Activity
charges.maxPenalty: Up to 20 years per racketeering count; life imprisonment if the racketeering includes murder; mandatory forfeiture of all proceeds and assets

charges.name: Money Laundering
charges.maxPenalty: Up to 20 years imprisonment; fines up to $500,000 or twice the value of the laundered funds; mandatory forfeiture of all laundered proceeds
